text:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT 1976123456 - elevated latency on streaming push endpoints observed in us-west-2. paging oncall (Sanjay Patel).
Sanjay Patel: I'm looking. p95 for push responses jumped from ~120ms to ~900ms in the last 6m.
Maria Gomez: seeing GPU queue depth climb on the serving fleet, memory inflight also up. non-streaming /sync endpoints are okay.
Eve Johnson: any correlated deploys?
Tim O'Neill: no deploys on main runtime in the last hour. looks like a traffic pattern shift — lots of long-lived streams.
Sanjay Patel: TL;DR: streaming keeps tokens alive and prevents batching efficiencies. need a live mitigation to drop tail latency. thinking: temporarily suppress push/streaming frames for hosted tier while we triage.
Maria Gomez: SGTM as an emergency mitigation. we should scope to hosted public API only, keep Dedicated/Private untouched. also prepare a communication note for support.
Eve Johnson: agree. plan: (1) flip streaming feature-flag off for public/hosted, (2) bump short-term rate limits on poll/complete endpoints for critical customers, (3) apply quota guard rails to avoid burst storms.
Sanjay Patel: I'm going to initiate feature toggle. tagging infra for rollout. PTAL @infra-bot.
infra-bot: queued: feature-toggle request received for feature=streaming_push, env=prod, scope=hosted-public. request id=ft-1976123456-1
Sanjay Patel: command I'm running:
```
curl -X POST https://ops-api.internal/feature-toggle \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"feature":"streaming_push","env":"prod","scope":"hosted-public","state":"off"}'
```
Maria Gomez: also run this to raise poll concurrency for top customers (names redacted):
```
# temporarily increase max_concurrent_requests for customers in group 'critical' by 20%
opsctl customer-config apply --group critical --set max_concurrent_requests=1.2x
```
deploy-bot: feature-toggle ft-1976123456-1 rolled out to edge control plane in 45s. Config propagation in progress.
infra-bot: edge-config version v2026.03.15-ft1976 applied. Target nodes: 120.
Sanjay Patel: rolling: disabling streaming on edge nodes now. will monitor.
Eve Johnson: heads up to support: customers on streaming will see immediate fallback to non-streaming responses — shorter token chunking and full-response delivery. prepare canned reply.
support-bot: creating ticket template: "We’ve temporarily suspended streaming responses to stabilize latency. You will receive full responses via immediate completion endpoints. We expect restoration within 30-60 minutes. If you rely on streaming for UX, please let us know and we’ll prioritize your case"
Maria Gomez: metrics update: p95 for push endpoints dropping from 900ms -> 220ms within 2m of toggle. GPU queue depth trending down.
Tim O'Neill: :white_check_mark: early signal looks good. error rates for completions + polling up ~2% — probably retries from clients. watching for customer 429s.
Sanjay Patel: I'm going to add a traffic-shaping rule to slow new long-lived connection accept rate by 30% to avoid re-saturation when we re-enable. Command:
```
opsctl traffic-shape add --route /v1/stream --mode accept-rate --ratio 0.7 --scope hosted-public
```
infra-bot: traffic-shape rule applied, id ts-1976123456-1.
Eve Johnson: who's owning customer comms? I'll coordinate with Support and Growth for a status banner. cc @Maria Gomez for technical blurb.
Maria Gomez: posting a short blurb: "We've temporarily suspended streaming responses for the hosted API to reduce latency for all customers. Non-streaming completions remain available and unaffected. We will re-enable streaming once latency is stable and GPU queues are drained."
Sanjay Patel: setting rollback criteria: re-enable when p95 < 250ms AND GPU queue depth < 15% for 10 consecutive minutes. also require no more than 2% error increase on completions.
Tim O'Neill: logging note: capture a sample of affected request ids for follow-up. `logs query "streaming.push" limit 200`
Maria Gomez: done. exported sample to s3://ops-incident-evidence/1976123456/evidence.json
Eve Johnson: handoff — I'm going offline in ~20m. Sanjay will be primary. Tim you take SRE backup.
Sanjay Patel: I'm primary. Tim O'Neill is backup. If condition worsens, escalate to on-call L4.
Sanjay Patel: current plan: maintain streaming off + traffic-shape + temporary rate uplift for critical customers. monitor 5m dashboards and error budget.
deploy-bot: status update: streaming_push=false applied globally to hosted-public edge proxies.
Maria Gomez: metric check at +10m: p95=210ms, GPU queue 9%, completion error +1.4%. Good.
Sanjay Patel: leaving note for re-enable steps and approval: require SMACK (SRE + ML runtime + infra + product) ack in thread before turning streaming back on.
Eve Johnson: filing follow-up tasks: incident postmortem, customer impact list, improve automatic detection for long-lived stream floods.
support-bot: flagged 18 incoming support threads referencing streaming interruptions, priority assigned: 6 high, 12 medium.
Sanjay Patel: leaving shift — Tim will watch for the next 30m then hand back. if thresholds met, Tim will request the SMACK approval to re-enable.
Tim O'Neill: copy. will monitor and post updates.
Sanjay Patel: :hourglass_flowing_sand: incident mitigated for now. keeping thread open for re-enable choreography and postmortem notes.
